messages:
maria (product): Quick sync: we need a concrete decision on the conversation endpoint shape for Q2. Key asks from customers: keep existing `prompt` for backward compat, add `messages` for structured UX, and a strict `system` role that can't be overridden by users. What can we ship without blowing up SDKs?

sam (eng): tl;dr we can support both payloads but need a compatibility layer. Main risk: runtime validation and ordering semantics for roles. If we accept both, we must define deterministic merge rules.

jordan (devex): UX-wise we should prefer `messages` as canonical in docs, but keep `prompt` as a migration shim. Provide auto-conversion tooling in SDKs. Also consider a lint/check tool to catch ambiguous role usage.

claire (research): customer evals show model behavior depends a lot on `system` placement and content. If we allow `system` in messages, we need strict guidance and examples to avoid regressions. Also, structured output + function calling interacts with role semantics.

elliot (security): note on restrictions: some enterprise customers want signed `system` content (policy), or at least an audittrail that system prompts were not user-injected. We should design metadata to tag system-origin.

maria (product): proposal: 1) Launch with `messages` first-class. 2) Accept `prompt` for compatibility and auto-convert to `messages` server-side with a deprecation plan (12 months). 3) Enforce a single `system` role that is treated specially (tagged, immutable once set). 4) Keep function calling and structured output unchanged but add docs on how roles interact. Thoughts?

sam (eng): Implementation notes: server-side conversion rules: if `prompt` is string -> becomes first `system` message by default, unless request provides an explicit `system` message in `messages`. If both exist, we must define precedence. Also need to update SDKs to surface warnings. Backwards compat test suite required.

jordan (devex): +1 to conversion rules, but defaulting `prompt` -> first `system` might surprise some apps. Can we instead create an explicit header `x-redwood-prompt-origin: prompt` when converted so devs can opt-in to old behavior? Also suggest a small sample migration script for common frameworks.

claire (research): For model behavior, converting `prompt` to `system` as the first message is sensible; it matches how many customers think about system prompts. Add a QA step: run prompt_sets against both payload shapes and detect divergence > threshold.

elliot (security): tagging is a must. Suggest `system_source: ["admin","converted_prompt","console"]` as metadata with values preserved in audit logs. That should satisfy enterprise compliance.

ops-bot: deployment note: canary for conversion layer rolled to 10% infra tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

maria (product): Launch criteria checklist draft: 1) RFC merged 2) SDK conversions shipped (py/ts) with deprecation warnings 3) Compatibility test suite with <1% behavior divergence on customers' evals 4) Audit tagging for system messages in logs 5) Docs + migration guide published. Any missing asks?

sam (eng): Also need an opt-out flag for customers who want strict legacy behavior (no auto-convert). Add `legacy_mode=true` feature flag on a per-tenant basis.

jordan (devex): Will write migration examples and a quick CLI tool for conversion. ETA 2 sprints.

claire (research): I'll run the regression harness on the top 25 customer prompt sets. Expect results in 5 days.

elliot (security): I'll draft the audit requirements and KMS/HSM implications for signed system prompts.

maria (product): Ok let's adopt this as the working plan. Action items: @sam implement conversion + flag, @jordan SDK + docs, @claire evals, @elliot audit. We'll track in the roadmap epic. :thumbsup:

sam (eng): noted. I'll add the conversion PR template and a short RFC for precedence rules.

jordan (devex): adding migration checklist to the docs repo now.

maria (product): Thanks team — reconvene after canary and eval results.
